educational_overlay.purpose: Distills complex multi-page judicial judgments into structured IRAC (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion) briefs.
educational_overlay.when_to_use: When reading landmark judgments, studying case law for moots, or preparing lecture summaries.
educational_overlay.when_not_to_use: As a substitute for reading primary judicial text when citing in appellate court.

variables.label: Full Case Citation
variables.default: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) 10 SCC 1

educational_overlay.prompt_template:
Prepare structured FILAC brief for judgment '{{CASE_NAME}}' decided by '{{BENCH_SIZE}}'.
Extract: (1) Material Facts, (2) Substantial Legal Issues, (3) Constitutional / Statutory Rules, (4) Ratio Decidendi & Judicial Reasoning, (5) Dissenting Views (if any), (6) Final Conclusion and Constitutional Impact.
Explicitly mark ratio vs obiter dicta.
educational_overlay.fictional_scenario: A law student must prepare a 2-page brief on the Right to Privacy judgment for a constitutional law seminar.
educational_overlay.sample_output:
### Case Brief: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
- **Issue**: Is the right to privacy a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution?
- **Rule**: Articles 14, 19, 21.
- **Ratio**: Privacy is a natural, inalienable right emanating from life and personal liberty under Article 21.
- **Test**: State interference must satisfy: (1) Legality, (2) Legitimate state aim, (3) Proportionality.
guardrails: Clearly distinguish between majority ratio and concurring obiter remarks.
verification_checklist: Verify whether judgment has been subsequently distinguished or overruled.
educational_overlay.ai_risk_warning: AI language models frequently confuse dissenting opinions with majority holdings.
